chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Khas'amy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who did not pause at Al-Muzdalifa and did not spend the night there until he went to Mina, he said: 'Did he not see the people and did he not acknowledge Mina when he entered it?' I said, 'If he was ignorant of that?' He said: 'He should return.' I said, 'If that opportunity has been lost?' He said: 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَة: Al-Muzdalifa, a sacred site where pilgrims gather after leaving Mina.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / no fault (indicating exemption from penalty).
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the tent city near Mecca where pilgrims stay.
key_terms.يَبِتْ: To spend the night (a ritual requirement at Al-Muzdalifa).
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: He should return (to perform the missed ritual).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to stand at Al-Muzdalifa during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling for a pilgrim who missed the obligatory standing (wuquf) at Al-Muzdalifa due to ignorance, distinguishing between those who can still return and those for whom the time has entirely passed. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the principle that ignorance of a ritual requirement does not incur penalty if the specific time window for the act has elapsed, emphasizing divine mercy in Hajj obligations. The narration underscores the practical flexibility within the Hajj rites, ensuring that pilgrims are not unduly burdened by minor omissions caused by lack of knowledge.
